proposals.before: Gaozu, temple name the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, was born to Niezhji. The family sprang from western tribes; they left the Zhuye for Tang service and settled with them in the Yin Mountains.
proposals.after: Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, was born to Niezhji. The family sprang from western tribes; they left the Zhuye for Tang service and settled with them in the Yin Mountains.
proposals.reason: Only Gaozu is the temple name; the following phrase is the emperor's extended honorific title.

proposals.before: Yan caught the column before it could form. Jingtang led barely a dozen riders in a slashing charge, took Yan prisoner, and broke clear.
proposals.after: Yan caught the column before it could form. Jingtang led barely a dozen riders in a slashing charge, brought Zhuangzong out, and broke clear.
proposals.reason: Chinese 取之以旋 describes Jingtang extracting the endangered ruler, not taking Liu Yan prisoner.

proposals.before: At Hulu Tao and Yangcun Mingzong met defeat; again and again Jingtang pulled him out of the killing ground.
proposals.after: At Hulu Tao and Yangcun, Mingzong met defeat; again and again Jingtang pulled him out of the killing ground.
proposals.reason: A missing comma fuses the place name Yangcun with Mingzong and obscures the subject.

proposals.before: Early in the second year, on guihai of the first month, Lu Wenzhi of Anyuan defected to Wu.
proposals.after: Early in the second year, on guihai of the first month, Lu Wenjin of Anyuan defected to Wu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese personal name is 盧文進 (Lu Wenjin), not Lu Wenzhi.

proposals.before: In spring of year 2, on guihai the first day of the first month, Lu Wenzhi, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and surrendered to Wu.
proposals.after: In spring of year 2, on guihai the first day of the first month, Lu Wenjin, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and surrendered to Wu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese personal name is 盧文進 (Lu Wenjin), not Lu Wenzhi.

proposals.before: Wang Yanchong, Lingzhou garrison commander, seized Huaiyuan and rose in revolt.
proposals.after: Wang Yanzhong, Lingzhou garrison commander, seized Huaiyuan and rose in revolt.
proposals.reason: The Chinese given name 彥忠 is Yanzhong; 'Yanchong' misreads 忠.

proposals.before: Wang Yanchong, garrison commander at Lingzhou, rebelled holding Huaiyuan city.
proposals.after: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander at Lingzhou, rebelled while holding Huaiyuan city.
proposals.reason: The Chinese given name 彥忠 is Yanzhong; 'Yanchong' misreads 忠.

proposals.before: On jiwei Yanchong submitted; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo then slew him.
proposals.after: On jiwei Yanzhong submitted; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo then slew him.
proposals.reason: The shortened name 彥忠 is Yanzhong, matching 王彥忠 in the preceding unit.

proposals.before: On jiwei Yanchong surrendered; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo killed him.
proposals.after: On jiwei Yanzhong surrendered; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo killed him.
proposals.reason: The shortened name 彥忠 is Yanzhong, matching 王彥忠 in the preceding unit.

proposals.before: Western tribes struck Jing; Zhang Yanzhe of Zhangyi drove them off and took their chief Yeliluoxiadú prisoner.
proposals.after: Western tribes struck Jing; Zhang Yanze of Zhangyi drove them off and took their chief Yeliluoxiadú prisoner.
proposals.reason: The Chinese personal name 張彥澤 is Zhang Yanze, not Zhang Yanzhe.

proposals.before: Western barbarians raided Jing; Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Zhangyi, defeated them and captured their leader Yeliluoxiadú.
proposals.after: Western barbarians raided Jing; Zhang Yanze, military governor of Zhangyi, defeated them and captured their leader Yeliluoxiadú.
proposals.reason: The Chinese personal name 張彥澤 is Zhang Yanze, not Zhang Yanzhe.

proposals.before: On yihai of the eleventh month shrines to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Deposed Emperor were raised in the Western Capital.
proposals.after: On yihai of the eleventh month shrines to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were raised in the Western Capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 湣帝 denotes Mindi (Emperor Min), not Congke, the Deposed Emperor.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month of winter, on yihai, temples to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Deposed Emperor were established in the Western Capital.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of winter, on yihai, temples to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were established in the Western Capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 湣帝 denotes Mindi (Emperor Min), not Congke, the Deposed Emperor.

proposals.before: On dingmao of the ninth month He Ning, Hanlin director and vice minister of revenue, entered the Chancellery as co-grand councilor.
proposals.after: On dingmao of the ninth month He Ning, Hanlin director and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.
proposals.reason: 中書侍郎 is vice director of the Secretariat; the current wording omits that office and substitutes the Chancellery.

proposals.before: In the ninth month, on dingmao, He Ning, Hanlin academician in charge and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Chancellery and co-grand councilor.
proposals.after: In the ninth month, on dingmao, He Ning, Hanlin academician in charge and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.
proposals.reason: 中書侍郎 belongs to the Secretariat, not the Chancellery.

proposals.before: On wuyin of the first month in the sixth year Tang Shuyu was made Prince of Xing’an and Tailu Duke of Changning.
proposals.after: On wuyin of the first month in the sixth year Tang Shuyu was made Prince of Xing’an and Tailu as Duke of Changning.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits ‘as’ before ‘Duke of Changning’, fusing Tailu with the title; the Chinese parallel 封…為… requires ‘as’, matching the literal field.

decisions.reason: Focus unit opens 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝: 高祖 alone is the temple name, and 聖文章武明德孝皇帝 is the posthumous honorific. Labeling that title “temple name” is wrong; the proposed wording drops the mislabel while keeping the rest intact.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝

decisions.reason: After 為掞所掩, 敬瑭…取之以旋 names no capture of Liu Yan; the next unit has 莊宗拊其背 praising Jingtang, so 之 is the endangered Zhuangzong. “Took Yan prisoner” invents an unstated capture; “brought Zhuangzong out” matches the rescue sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 敬瑭以十餘騎橫槊馳擊，取之以旋

decisions.reason: Chinese 明宗戰胡盧套、楊村，為梁兵所敗 is already clear in the original idiomatic English; adding a comma after Yangcun is only stylistic and does not correct meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 明宗戰胡盧套、楊村，為梁兵所敗

decisions.reason: Focus unit names 盧文進; 文進 is Wenjin, not Wenzhi. The proposed idiomatic name corrects that reading error without other changes.
The same 盧文進 in the focus unit requires Lu Wenjin in the literal field; replacing Wenzhi restores the Chinese personal name.
Focus unit has 王彥忠; 忠 is zhong, so Yanchong misreads the given name. Wang Yanzhong is the correct reading.
Literal English likewise misreads 彥忠 as Yanchong; Yanzhong matches 王彥忠, and “rebelled while holding Huaiyuan city” still renders 以懷遠城反.
Short form 彥忠 in this unit is the same person as 王彥忠 in s0117; idiomatic Yanchong must be Yanzhong.
Literal 彥忠 likewise requires Yanzhong to match the preceding 王彥忠; the rest of the surrender wording is already accurate.
Focus unit names 張彥澤; 澤 is ze, so Yanzhe is a wrong reading. Zhang Yanze restores the Chinese personal name.
The literal field has the same 張彥澤 misread as Yanzhe; correcting to Yanze matches the Chinese without changing the rest.
Focus unit lists 湣帝 among the Tang emperors honored; that is Emperor Min (Mindi), not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝, Congke). “Emperor Min” restores the correct identity.
Literal English likewise renders 湣帝 as the Deposed Emperor; Emperor Min matches 湣帝 and distinguishes him from Congke.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 立唐高祖、太宗、莊宗、明宗、湣帝廟於西京

decisions.reason: He Ning is appointed 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事: 中書侍郎 is vice director of the Secretariat, not entry into the Chancellery. The proposed wording restores both the office and the co-grand councilorship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 和凝為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事

decisions.reason: Literal “vice director of the Chancellery” misassigns 中書侍郎; Secretariat is required, matching the Chinese office title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事

decisions.reason: Chinese 封唐叔虞為興安王，臺駘為昌寧公 enfeoffs two recipients in parallel. Without “as” before Duke of Changning, Tailu can fuse into Tang Shuyu’s titles; inserting “as” restores the two separate grants.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封唐叔虞為興安王，臺駘為昌寧公
